name: NanoLimbo-rs (Debian)
author: r.makeev@flipper.net
description: A tiny, fast Minecraft limbo server written in Rust. Keeps players connected while your real server restarts - 51 protocol versions, Minecraft 1.7.2 (protocol 4) through 26.2 (protocol 776), from one static binary and a few megabytes of RAM.

installation.script:
#!/bin/sh
# NanoLimbo-rs Installation Script
set -e

apt-get update
apt-get install -y curl jq

UNAME_M="$(uname -m)"
case "$UNAME_M" in
  x86_64)   ARCH='x86_64' ;;
  aarch64)  ARCH='aarch64' ;;
  *)
    echo "ERROR: Unsupported arch: $UNAME_M" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

GITHUB_PACKAGE="Astra-Interactive/NanoLimbo-rs"
PATTERN="nanolimbo_linux-${ARCH}-gnu[.]tar[.]gz"

select_asset_url() {
  jq -r --arg pat "$PATTERN" '
    .assets[].browser_download_url
    | select(test($pat))
  '
}

# The panel patches settings.yml line by line, so both bind keys must be present at the
# indentation the shipped file uses, or the server would ignore its allocation.
has_patchable_bind() {
  grep -q '^  ip: ' settings.yml && grep -q '^  port: ' settings.yml
}

echo "Fetching GitHub releases metadata..."
ALL_JSON="$(curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/$GITHUB_PACKAGE/releases")"
LATEST_JSON="$(printf '%s\n' "$ALL_JSON" \
  | jq 'map(select(.prerelease==false)) | sort_by(.published_at) | reverse | .[0]')"

# Release tags are bare workspace versions, without a 'v' prefix (e.g. 0.3.0). The ref is
# used to fetch the settings.yml that ships with the very binary being installed.
SETTINGS_REF="master"

if [ -n "$DOWNLOAD_URL" ]; then
  echo "Using provided DOWNLOAD_URL"
  if ! curl -Isf "$DOWNLOAD_URL" >/dev/null; then
    echo "ERROR: Provided download URL is invalid." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

elif [ -n "$VERSION" ] && [ "$VERSION" != "latest" ]; then
  echo "Looking for tag '$VERSION'..."
  MATCH="$(printf '%s\n' "$ALL_JSON" \
    | jq -c --arg v "$VERSION" '.[] | select(.tag_name==$v)')"
  if [ -n "$MATCH" ]; then
    DOWNLOAD_URL="$(printf '%s\n' "$MATCH" | select_asset_url)"
    SETTINGS_REF="$VERSION"
  else
    echo "Warning: tag '$VERSION' not found, falling back to latest stable."
    DOWNLOAD_URL="$(printf '%s\n' "$LATEST_JSON" | select_asset_url)"
    SETTINGS_REF="$(printf '%s\n' "$LATEST_JSON" | jq -r '.tag_name // "master"')"
  fi

else
  echo "Selecting latest stable release..."
  DOWNLOAD_URL="$(printf '%s\n' "$LATEST_JSON" | select_asset_url)"
  SETTINGS_REF="$(printf '%s\n' "$LATEST_JSON" | jq -r '.tag_name // "master"')"
fi

if [ -z "$DOWNLOAD_URL" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: No release asset matching '$PATTERN' was found." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

SERVER_BINARY=${SERVER_BINARY:-nanolimbo}
ARCHIVE=${DOWNLOAD_URL##*/}

echo "Downloading $ARCHIVE ..."
curl -sSL -o "$ARCHIVE" "$DOWNLOAD_URL"

echo "Extracting..."
tar -xzf "$ARCHIVE"
rm "$ARCHIVE"

chmod +x "$SERVER_BINARY"

# The server has no command line flags: it reads settings.yml from its working directory
# and writes the shipped default there when the file is missing. That default binds
# localhost:65535, and the panel only rewrites a file that already exists - so without
# this step the first boot would come up on the wrong port, unreachable from outside the
# container. Fetching the file instead of embedding it keeps one source of truth.
if [ ! -f settings.yml ]; then
  echo "Installing default settings.yml ..."
  SETTINGS_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$GITHUB_PACKAGE/$SETTINGS_REF/crates/limbo-config/resources/settings.yml"
  if ! curl -sSLf -o settings.yml "$SETTINGS_URL" || ! has_patchable_bind; then
    echo "Warning: could not fetch the documented default, writing a minimal one."
    printf '%s\n' \
      '# The panel rewrites both values below on every boot.' \
      '# Every other setting falls back to its built-in default; the fully documented' \
      '# file lives at crates/limbo-config/resources/settings.yml in the source tree.' \
      'bind:' \
      '  ip: "0.0.0.0"' \
      '  port: 25565' > settings.yml
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installed NanoLimbo-rs -> /mnt/server/$SERVER_BINARY"
echo "-----------------------------------------"
